mainTopic: The הלכה on the צרה of an אילונית, a ברייתא on women who use a מוך, and whether a minor can give birth
overview: The amud opens with the final הלכה on the earlier discussion: the צרה of an אילונית may marry the יבם, even if the husband knew of her condition. To fit this ruling, the גמרא changes the משנה's word 'שנמצאו' to 'שהיו'. רבין then reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the צרות of a ממאנת, an אילונית and a man who remarried his divorcée are all permitted. Next, רב ביבי teaches a ברייתא listing three women who use a מוך because pregnancy would be dangerous: a קטנה, a pregnant woman and a nursing woman. רבי מאיר defines the endangered קטנה as a girl aged eleven and a day to twelve and a day, while the חכמים say all these women live normally and rely on 'שומר פתאים ה׳'. The ברייתא's words 'perhaps she will die' seem to allow a minor to give birth, which would make possible a חמות who did מיאון, and the משנה says that cannot happen. The גמרא tries rereading the ברייתא and brings support from רבה בר ליואי, but רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא pushes it back to the original wording. רב ספרא then answers that having children counts as signs of adulthood, so a mother is no longer a minor who can do מיאון. A second version says children are even better than signs, and the practical difference is that even רבי יהודה agrees about children.

steps.title: The final ruling: the co-wife of an אילונית is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that the צרה of an אילונית may marry the יבם. This holds even if the husband knew she was an אילונית, and even when the אילונית is the יבם's own daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: the co-wife of an אילונית is permitted, even if the husband knew about her condition, and even the co-wife of his own daughter who is an אילונית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the earlier discussion about the צרה of an אילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אילונית (a woman who cannot have children) does not fall to יבום, so her צרה is not treated as the 'co-wife of an ערוה'. The ruling goes further than we might expect: even when the husband knew about her condition and married her anyway, the צרה is still permitted. It also applies when the אילונית is the יבם's daughter, which is the classic case of צרת ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה; the final ruling
A co-wife; another wife of the same husband
A woman who cannot have children

steps.whatToRemember: The צרה of an אילונית is permitted, even if the husband knew, and even when the אילונית is the יבם's daughter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for the earlier back-and-forth about the אילונית.

phrases.english: The halakha is: the rival wife of an aylonit is permitted,
and even if he knew about her.
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband, who knew she was an אילונית when he married her.

phrases.english: And even the rival wife of his daughter who is an aylonit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion about the אילונית with a final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The צרה of an אילונית is permitted in every case, even if the husband knew of her condition.

steps.title: What about the משנה's word 'were found to be'?
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling applies even when the husband knew, why does the משנה say 'שנמצאו', which sounds like he only found out later?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the משנה, which says 'that were found to be' (אילוניות)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling from Step 1 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the צרות are permitted when the wives 'were found to be' אילוניות. That word suggests the husband discovered it only after the wedding. If so, the משנה seems to permit the צרה only when he did not know, which goes against the ruling that she is permitted 'even if he knew'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That were found to be', meaning discovered later

phrases.english: But then, that which it teaches, "that were found to be"?
phrases.notes: This is the first משנה of the מסכת, which speaks of wives who "were found to be" אילוניות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of Step 1 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the צרה is permitted even if the husband knew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word 'שנמצאו' implies the rule applies only when the condition was discovered later.

steps.title: Read the משנה as 'that were'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה should read 'שהיו' ('that were') instead of 'שנמצאו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'שהיו', the משנה just says the wives were אילוניות. It says nothing about when the husband found out. So the משנה no longer conflicts with the ruling that the צרה is permitted even if he knew.

phrases.english: Teach: "that were."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שנמצאו' suggests the husband did not know, so the rule would be limited to that case
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה reads 'שהיו', so the rule covers every אילונית, whether he knew or not

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: three kinds of co-wives are all permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that three צרות are all permitted. They are the צרה of a ממאנת, the צרה of an אילונית, and the צרה of a man who remarried his divorcée.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the co-wife of a girl who refused, the co-wife of an אילונית, and the co-wife of a man who took back his divorcée are all permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement from ארץ ישראל that agrees with the ruling and groups three cases together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each of these three cases, the woman who is an ערוה to the יבם is not treated as his brother's wife who falls to יבום. A ממאנת's marriage is undone by her refusal, and an אילונית does not fall to יבום. In the third case, the marriage after the divorce is forbidden. Since she is not treated as a wife falling to יבום, her צרה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When רבין came' from ארץ ישראל to בבל
A girl married as a minor who refuses her husband (מיאון)
A man who takes back his divorced wife after she married someone else

steps.whatToRemember: ממאנת, אילונית, מחזיר גרושתו: in all three cases the צרה is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Both the rival wife of a girl who refused,
and the rival wife of an aylonit,
and the rival wife of one who takes back his divorcée —
they are all permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the ruling of Step 1 and adds two similar cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צרות of a ממאנת, an אילונית, and a man who remarried his divorcée are all permitted.

steps.title: Three women who use a מוך
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי teaches a ברייתא: a קטנה, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman use a מוך, because a pregnancy could put someone in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי taught before רב נחמן: three women use a pad during relations. They are a minor, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman. The minor, because she might get pregnant and die. The pregnant woman, because her fetus might become flattened like a סנדל fish. The nursing woman, because she might have to wean her baby early and he could die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא listing three women who use a מוך, with the danger behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a מוך is not normally done. These three women are an exception because a pregnancy would be dangerous. For the minor, the danger is to her own life. For the pregnant woman, a second pregnancy could crush the fetus she is already carrying. For the nursing woman, a new pregnancy could dry up her milk and endanger her baby.

keyTerms.meaning: A soft pad of cloth used to prevent pregnancy

steps.confusionAlert: Commentators disagree whether this means these women are allowed to use a מוך or are required to. The plain words just say they 'use' one.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rav Beivai taught before Rav Naḥman:
Three women engage in relations with a resorbent pad:
a minor, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman.
A minor — lest she become pregnant and perhaps die.
A pregnant woman — lest her fetus become a sandal.
phrases.notes: The worry is a second pregnancy pressing on the first baby and flattening it.

phrases.english: A nursing woman — lest she wean her son and he die.
phrases.notes: A new pregnancy could dry up her milk, forcing her to stop nursing too early.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, connected to the young girl (the ממאנת) mentioned in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטנה, a מעוברת, and a מניקה use a מוך because pregnancy would be dangerous.

steps.title: רבי מאיר defines the 'minor'
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the קטנה in danger is a girl from age 11 and a day until 12 and a day. Younger or older girls have relations normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the 'minor'? A girl from eleven years and one day until twelve years and one day. Younger or older than this, she has relations in the normal way. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains exactly which girl counts as the 'minor' in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below 11, she cannot become pregnant, so there is no danger. Above 12, her body can safely carry a pregnancy. Only the one-year window in between is risky, so only then does she use a מוך.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And which one is...', asking for a definition

phrases.english: And who is the minor?

phrases.aramaic: מִבַּת אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: From the age of eleven years and one day

phrases.aramaic: עַד שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: until twelve years and one day.
Less than this or more than this —
she goes ahead and has relations in her usual manner,
the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a girl aged 11 and a day to 12 and a day uses a מוך; others have relations normally.

steps.title: The חכמים: all live normally and Heaven protects
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. They say all these women have relations normally and trust Heaven to protect them, based on the פסוק 'שומר פתאים ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: both this one and that one have relations in the normal way, and Heaven will have mercy, as it says: 'ה׳ protects the simple.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue on רבי מאיר and say no special precaution is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the women at risk use a מוך. The חכמים say they live normally, because ordinary people who cannot fully guard against rare dangers are protected by ה׳. They bring a פסוק to support this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the חכמים say', the opposing view

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the women at risk use a מוך. חכמים: they live normally and rely on 'שומר פתאים ה׳'.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Both this one and that one
phrases.notes: This means the women רבי מאיר called at risk and the ones he didn't, so all of them.

phrases.english: go ahead and have relations in the usual manner,
and Heaven will have mercy,
since it is stated: "The Lord preserves the simple."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All women have relations normally; Heaven protects them (שומר פתאים ה׳).

steps.title: Inference from the ברייתא contradicts the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's words 'and perhaps she will die' imply that some minors become pregnant and live. That would make a חמות who did מיאון possible, which the משנה says cannot happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the ברייתא says 'lest she become pregnant and perhaps die,' it must be that some minor girls get pregnant and don't die. If so, we can have a mother-in-law who did מיאון. But the משנה taught that you cannot say a mother-in-law, her mother, or a father-in-law's mother was an אילונית or did מיאון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא from step 5 closely and finds that it seems to clash with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'perhaps' means death is not certain, so some pregnant minors survive. If a minor can give birth and live, her daughter could marry a man while the mother is still a minor, and the mother could then do מיאון. The משנה says this case is impossible, so the ברייתא and the משנה contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; it follows from this
A girl who does מיאון, refusing a marriage her family arranged while she was a minor
A woman who cannot have children

steps.confusionAlert: Only a minor can do מיאון. So the whole question is whether a girl could already be a mother while still a minor.

phrases.english: From the fact that it says: lest she become pregnant
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא of רב ביבי about the מוך, from step 5.

phrases.english: and perhaps she will die,
this implies that there is a minor girl
who becomes pregnant and does not die.
If so, we find a mother-in-law who refused.
phrases.notes: She gave birth as a minor, her baby daughter married him, and then the mother herself did מיאון.

phrases.english: But we learned in the משנה: You cannot say
regarding his mother-in-law, his mother-in-law's mother, and his father-in-law's mother
that they were found to be an אילונית or that they refused!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר שֶׁמָּא תִּתְעַבֵּר וְשֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת, מִכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of רב ביבי's ברייתא and sets it against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's wording 'ושמא תמות' as compared with the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'perhaps' implies that some minors survive pregnancy. That makes a minor mother-in-law who does מיאון possible, which the משנה rules out.

steps.title: Read the ברייתא as 'become pregnant and die'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the ברייתא's wording: if a minor becomes pregnant, she will certainly die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: lest she become pregnant and die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא no longer says 'perhaps she will die.' Only the pregnancy is uncertain, and if it happens, death is certain. So no minor ever gives birth and survives, and the משנה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (read the text this way)

phrases.english: Say instead:
lest she become pregnant and die.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא said that a pregnant minor only perhaps dies.
steps.terutzMaskana: A pregnant minor certainly dies, so a minor mother is impossible.

steps.title: רבה בר ליואי: the three stages of a young girl's pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר ליואי says that before a certain age a girl cannot conceive, during that age she and the baby die, and after it they both live.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר ליואי said: There is a limit for her. Before this time, she cannot get pregnant at all. During this time, she dies and her baby dies. After this time, she lives and her baby lives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the new reading 'become pregnant and die.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר ליואי's stages leave no time when a minor gives birth and lives. Before the stage she cannot conceive, during it she dies, and by the time she survives she is no longer a minor who can do מיאון. This fits exactly with 'she will become pregnant and die.'

keyTerms.meaning: A limit or boundary (here, of age)

phrases.english: As Rabba bar Livai said:
She has a limit,
before this time —
phrases.notes: 'This time' seems to be the danger age from step 6, from 11 and a day until 12 and a day.

phrases.english: she cannot become pregnant at all;
during this time —
she dies and her fetus dies;
after this time —
she lives and her fetus lives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the new wording given in step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבה בר ליואי about the three age stages

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא suggests a minor can give birth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that a חמות cannot do מיאון 'because they already gave birth.' This implies that the problem is only that she gave birth, not that giving birth as a minor is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבה בר שמואל taught: You cannot say that a mother-in-law, her mother, or a father-in-law's mother was an אילונית or did מיאון, because they already gave birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading with a ברייתא that seems to assume a minor can give birth and live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If minors could never give birth, the reason would be 'because they are already adults.' Instead the reason given is 'because they already gave birth.' That seems to say that giving birth, not adulthood, is what ends the possibility of מיאון. So a minor can give birth, which goes against step 9 and רבה בר ליואי.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabba bar Shmuel teach:
You cannot say
regarding his mother-in-law, his mother-in-law's mother, and his father-in-law's mother
that they were found to be an אילונית or that they refused —
because they already gave birth.
phrases.notes: The point is the wording. He didn't say 'because they're already grown up,' so it sounds like a minor can give birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9 and the support from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'שמא תתעבר ותמות' and the view of רבה בר ליואי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason 'because they already gave birth' implies that birth, not adulthood, rules out מיאון. So minors can give birth and survive.

steps.title: Back to the original wording, and the משנה remains difficult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to 'lest she become pregnant and perhaps die' and admits that this brings back the difficulty against the משנה. רב ספרא answers it in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really: lest she become pregnant and perhaps die. But then that משנה is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its change of wording and goes back to the original text of the ברייתא. This brings back the problem with the משנה, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא, the original wording 'perhaps die' is kept, meaning some minors survive pregnancy. That brings back the problem from step 8: a חמות who did מיאון becomes possible, against the משנה. רב ספרא answers this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (going back to the original idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא keeps its original wording, 'perhaps she will die,' so some minors can give birth and survive. This brings back the קשיא against the משנה, which says a חמות can never be a ממאנת. The next step answers it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא הך' here re-opens the difficulty. It does not end the discussion: רב ספרא answers it right away in the next step.

phrases.english: Rather, actually:
lest she become pregnant and perhaps die.
But then that one is difficult!
phrases.notes: 'That one' is our משנה, which says a mother-in-law can't have done מיאון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם: שֶׁמָּא תִּתְעַבֵּר וְשֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת. וְאֶלָּא קַשְׁיָא הָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 11, drops the answer of step 9, and brings back the קשיא of step 8, which step 13 answers.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The original wording of the ברייתא stands, which brings back the contradiction with the משנה. Step 13 answers it.

steps.title: Having children counts as signs of adulthood
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers the difficulty from step 12. A girl who gave birth is treated as having the signs of adulthood, so she is no longer a minor and cannot do מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: Children are like signs of adulthood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא answers the leftover difficulty against the משנה. He says that giving birth works like the physical signs of adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that if a minor could give birth and live, she could become a חמות and then do מיאון. רב ספרא says that once she gives birth, she counts as an adult. A grown woman cannot do מיאון, so the משנה's rule that a חמות never does מיאון still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Children. Here it means the fact that she has given birth.
Signs of physical maturity, usually two hairs, that make a girl a legal adult.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
Children are like signs of adulthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: בָּנִים הֲרֵי הֵם כְּסִימָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא re-raised in step 12, the original problem from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the girl's status: giving birth itself makes her an adult.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A minor who gave birth stays a minor, so she could become a חמות and still do מיאון, against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Giving birth equals signs of adulthood, so she is an adult and cannot do מיאון. The משנה stands.

steps.title: A second version: children are even better than signs
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רב ספרא's statement says that children are stronger proof of adulthood than the physical signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: Children are better than signs of adulthood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב ספרא's answer. In this version, giving birth is an even stronger proof of adulthood than the signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that a girl who gave birth is no longer a minor, so the difficulty is answered either way. The second version adds that birth is more certain proof than hairs. This prepares the next question about what difference the two versions make.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say. This introduces another version of a statement.

phrases.english: And some say:
Children are better than signs of adulthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the answer in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same answer as step 13, but it rates giving birth higher than the signs.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving birth is only equal to signs.
steps.terutzMaskana: Giving birth is a stronger proof of adulthood than signs.

steps.title: What difference do the two versions make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between 'equal to signs' and 'better than signs.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under both versions a girl who gave birth is an adult. So the גמרא wants to know in what case calling birth 'better' than signs would change the law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference? Literally, 'what comes out of it?'

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two versions in steps 13 and 14 differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where 'children equal signs' and 'children are better than signs' would lead to different laws.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה agrees about children
steps.stepSummary: The difference concerns רבי יהודה, who needs more than two hairs for adulthood. According to the second version, even he agrees that giving birth makes her an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is that even רבי יהודה, who said a girl can do מיאון until the black hair is plentiful, agrees that once she has children she is an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two versions differ according to רבי יהודה. He requires a lot of hair before a girl stops being able to do מיאון, but he agrees that children settle the matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that two hairs are not enough, and a girl can still do מיאון until the black hair covers more area. If children were only 'like signs,' birth might be treated like two hairs, which is not enough for him. The version that says children are 'better' teaches that even רבי יהודה agrees birth makes her fully an adult.

keyTerms.meaning: Until the black (hair) becomes plentiful, covering more than the bare skin.

steps.whatToRemember: A girl who gave birth is an adult and cannot do מיאון, so a חמות who does מיאון cannot happen. According to the version that says 'children are better than signs,' even רבי יהודה, who needs many hairs, agrees.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה disagrees with רב ספרא's answer. The point is that birth works even according to him, while two hairs alone would not.

phrases.english: That even according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who said 'until the black is plentiful,'
phrases.notes: Even after two hairs a girl can still do מיאון, until the black hair covers more than the bare skin.

phrases.english: in the case of children he agrees.
phrases.notes: He agrees that once she has had children she is an adult and can no longer do מיאון.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר עַד שֶׁיִּרְבֶּה הַשָּׁחוֹר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The versions differ according to רבי יהודה. If children are 'better than signs,' even he agrees that a girl who gave birth is an adult, though he would not count two hairs.
